question.text: A call option seller receives Rs 10 premium on a zinc call with strike Rs 180. If the market price at expiry is Rs 220, the call seller's net loss is:

explanation.text: The Logic: Call seller net loss = (Market - Strike) - Premium received = (220 - 180) - 10 = 40 - 10 = Rs 30 net loss, matching the seller-loss row in the workbook table. The Trap: Rs 40 is the gross obligation before netting the premium. Rs 10 is just the premium received. Rs 20 ignores the full premium offset. Only Rs 30 nets the Rs 10 premium against the Rs 40 gross loss. Note: The workbook describes a short call's maximum risk as unlimited because losses grow with rising market prices, with the premium being the only offset.
